Nattokinase saved my life a few years ago. You should probably consider taking it.🧵NK is a cheap, powerful, and easy to get fibrinolytic that dissolves blood clots and plaques. Imo it’s also the supplement with the best +EV for longevity and cognitive health. (1/n)

===

1707082047678722480 [2023-09-27] @johnsonmxe 💜 46 🔁 1
A few years ago I had some mysterious symptoms — strange yellowing bruises (especially after flying) despite not bumping into anything, a strange “hot ripping pain” just above my knees, sharp pinprick pains that traveled periodically, strange sluggishness, and eventually cardiovascular issues. A doctor visit showed my D-dimer was elevated. Tried aspirin, long walks, pineapple juice (apparently a mild fibrinolytic). Every day was worse. Tried nattokinase — noticeably better after the first day. After a week, my symptoms were gone.
↓
1707082196865945790 [2023-09-27] @johnsonmxe 💜 61 🔁 2
I think being familiar with what it feels like to have clots — and that nattokinase is a viable treatment for them — is among the most unusual pieces of health knowledge I have. I’d like more people to have this knowledge.
↓
1707082453121171555 [2023-09-27] @johnsonmxe 💜 36 🔁 1
I expect clots can lead to a dynamic similar to “Kessler syndrome” — basically, if a blood clot is banging around in your vascular system, it can create injuries that lead to more clots, which then go on to make more clots, and so on. Not great. The good news is that if you reverse this by giving the body extra help in dissolving clots, it can clear up very rapidly and not come back.https://t.co/PfvHOf7ZP1
↓
1707083562367725866 [2023-09-27] @johnsonmxe 💜 37
What should people expect from taking NK? Mostly, nattokinase supplementation is about ‘the dog that didn’t bark’. Fewer bad things happen, especially if you’re still eating seed oils (apparently a substantial contributor to microclots)But I felt healthier after taking… https://t.co/y7m1mJXyCd

1707083699290853679 [2023-09-27] @johnsonmxe 💜 32 🔁 3
A couple friends report feeling “good but weird” after taking nattokinase. I suspect this could be because the vascular system gets calibrated to a certain flexibility. If you have a lot of plaques and other debris that stiffen your vascular system and then take nattokinase, some of these dissolve and your vasculature will regain some flexibility. This generally feels good, but the pressure shifts can be disconcerting until your system recalibrates.

  [Quoting @ahandvanish: Study looking at non-hospitalized, young adults (~age 19-21) with COVID found higher carotid artery stiffness & aortic stiffness vs controls.   Carotid artery = brain's main blood supply; stiffness associated w' cardiovascular disease, stroke, cognitive dysfunction #LongCovid 1/ https://t.co/g1QBxRMjjM]

1707084107421732911 [2023-09-27] @johnsonmxe 💜 30
I’m not a doctor and this isn’t medical advice, just my story. Counterindications for nattokinase include head trauma, having a known blood disorder that hinders clotting, or taking other blood thinners. It’s always possible someone has a big clot that’s lodged somewhere, and taking a fibrinolytic will dissolve it enough that it floats free and gets caught somewhere more serious.
↓
1707084228070969484 [2023-09-27] @johnsonmxe 💜 42
But for the average person I think nattokinase is hugely positive. It’s probably especially good to supplement if you have symptoms of clots, are a frequent traveler, have a history of cardiovascular disease / poor diet / arterial plaque, have COVID, are recovering from covid, or have recently taken a covid vaccine.But I think even “healthy” people would likely benefit from a bit more fibrinolysis. *Especially* in the era of covid.
